top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities as vectors with magnitude and direction.
Add and decompose vectors in two dimensions using components and right-triangle relationships.
Apply vector components to explain and predict two-dimensional projectile motion.
Relate launch speed and angle to trajectory, range, and maximum height in ideal projectile motion.

scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the idea that some physical quantities require both size and direction.
key_visuals: A tabletop or floor reference plane with x- and y-axes overlaid
Several arrows of different lengths and orientations labeled as displacement or velocity
A comparison between a scalar value and a vector arrow
student_actions: Inspect and compare arrows with different magnitudes and directions
Identify which displayed quantities are vectors and describe each by length and angle

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how two vectors combine geometrically to form a resultant.
key_visuals: Two movable arrows placed tip-to-tail on a coordinate grid
A resultant arrow drawn from the start of the first vector to the end of the second
A contrasting view showing the same vectors translated without changing their values
student_actions: Reposition vectors tip-to-tail
Predict and then observe the resultant vector
Compare how changing one vector changes the resultant

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect a vector’s magnitude and direction to its horizontal and vertical components.
key_visuals: A single vector at an angle from the horizontal
Dashed projection lines to the x- and y-axes forming a right triangle
Labeled component arrows for x and y
student_actions: Decompose the angled vector into horizontal and vertical parts
Read or estimate the component values
Relate the vector’s angle and magnitude to the component lengths

scenes.scene_name: From Components Back to Magnitude and Direction
scenes.brief_purpose: Reinforce that components fully determine the original vector through right-triangle relationships.
key_visuals: Separate x and y component arrows on a grid
A reconstructed diagonal vector completing the right triangle
Displayed links among component lengths, resultant magnitude, and angle
student_actions: Rebuild a vector from given components
Estimate the magnitude and direction from the component pair
Check how changing one component affects the final vector

scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the initial velocity of a projectile.
key_visuals: A launcher sending a ball out at an adjustable speed and angle
The initial velocity vector drawn at the launch point
Horizontal and vertical velocity components shown beside the launch vector
student_actions: Adjust launch angle and speed
Observe how the initial velocity splits into horizontal and vertical components
Predict which component will control forward motion and which will control rise and fall

scenes.scene_name: Independence of Horizontal and Vertical Motion
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate that horizontal motion remains uniform while vertical motion changes under gravity.
key_visuals: A projectile trajectory with synchronized horizontal and vertical component views
Equal-time position markers along the path
A constant horizontal velocity indicator and a changing vertical velocity indicator with downward gravity arrow
student_actions: Step through the motion at equal time intervals
Compare horizontal spacing with changes in vertical motion
Explain why horizontal and vertical behaviors differ during flight

scenes.scene_name: Connecting Components to the Parabolic Path
scenes.brief_purpose: Show how constant horizontal motion plus uniformly accelerated vertical motion produces the full trajectory.
key_visuals: The complete parabolic path traced through space
A side-by-side or overlaid view of horizontal motion, vertical motion, and combined motion
Markers for maximum height, range, and symmetric points about the peak
student_actions: Link the separate component motions to the combined path
Identify where vertical velocity becomes zero and how that relates to maximum height
Describe how the shape of the trajectory emerges from the two component motions

scenes.scene_name: Exploring How Launch Conditions Change the Outcome
scenes.brief_purpose: Let students generalize how launch speed and angle affect range and maximum height.
key_visuals: Multiple projectile paths for different launch angles and speeds
Comparative markers showing different ranges and peak heights
A resettable graph or table summarizing outcomes for each trial
student_actions: Run several launches with varied angle and speed
Compare trajectories to determine trends in range and height
Form a qualitative rule relating launch conditions to projectile behavior
